theme: Setup B R-multiple distribution — sizing the wide-body green 9:30 + high retest trade
builds_on: analyses/930-followthrough (which found wide-body green 9:30 + high retest closes green 76.92% of the time)

setup_definition.entry: 9:30 high price (oh) at first retest in 9:45-10:00 bar

summary.headline_finding: Despite the 76.92% 'day closes green' rate, holding to close with a 1R stop at the 9:30 low produces a slightly NEGATIVE expected R (-0.12R). The path to the green close goes through significant drawdown — average MAE is 1.33R, and 44% of trades get stopped at -1R.

MFE_distribution_peak_in_favor.interpretation: Modest favorable move but didn't reach +1R

key_findings.1: The 76.92% 'day-closes-green' stat from 930-followthrough is misleading for trade sizing. With a 1R stop at the 9:30 low, you get stopped out 44% of the time — even on days that eventually close green.
key_findings.2: Average MAE (peak adverse excursion) is 1.33R — meaning the AVERAGE trade goes 1.33x the 9:30 range against entry at some point. The 9:30 low is too tight a stop for this setup.
key_findings.3: Average MFE (peak favorable) is 1.07R — when trades work, they work nicely. ~46% of trades reach 1R+ in favor at some point.
key_findings.4: Final R held to close: -0.12R on average. Strategy is unprofitable as defined. The 'green close' rate doesn't translate into positive R because winners are smaller than losers.
key_findings.5: Best trade structure (suggested, not tested): wider stop OR earlier take-profit. With a 0.5R take-profit, ~82% of trades reach that level (only the 0-0.5R MFE bucket = 18% wouldn't trigger). But sequencing of MFE vs MAE matters — if MAE happens first, the take-profit never triggers.

limitations.intra_bar_sequencing_not_tracked: The Pine indicator records peak MFE and peak MAE separately, but does not capture which came first within a bar. For accurate trade simulation with stops and targets, intra-bar tick data would be needed.
limitations.sample_size: n=39 setups in 232-day window. Confidence interval on the 43.59% stop-out rate is roughly ±15pp. Headline conclusions are directional, not precise.
